clue.text: One not totally behind meeting without consultation

indicators.note: not totally means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
behind, as in behind schedule, means late
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't fully back a meeting, or a decision taken by one party alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' drops the last letter of UNIT, leaving UNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting unilaterally means acting alone, with no consultation of other parties.

clue.text: Not gratified being deposed, losing fourth place

indicators.note: losing fourth place means the letter in position four drops out

parts.note: being deposed means being unseated from power

explanation.surface: A ruler, unhappy at being overthrown and dropping down the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsated means not satisfied, with appetite or desire unfulfilled.

clue.text: Fare in Delhi halving … that is ridiculous

indicators.note: halving means splitting the other piece in two by sitting in its middle

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
nan is Indian flatbread, food eaten in Delhi

explanation.surface: Splitting a meal in Delhi presented as absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halving' means NAN cuts IE in two. NAN is a spelling of naan bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and senseless, so ridiculous.

clue.text: Area with sheep circling around for drink

indicators.note: circling means going round another piece

parts.note: a merino is a breed of sheep
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: A farmer's sheep wander around a field looking for water.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is a coffee drink of espresso diluted with hot water.

clue.text: Upset offended deity

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned up, read from the bottom

parts.note: sore means offended or aggrieved

explanation.surface: An offended god, upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: 25 this peculiar could become incomparable

indicators.note: could become means the combined letters may be rearranged into the other word

parts.note: the answer to 25 down is epic

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue claiming something odd could turn matchless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EPIC (25) plus the answer rearrange to INCOMPARABLE; 'this' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means unusual or out of the ordinary, so peculiar.

clue.text: Clues where northerner might be from, by listening

indicators.note: by listening means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Leeds is a city in the north of England

explanation.surface: Detective-style hints about a northerner's home town, picked up by eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS is a major city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leads are clues, pieces of information pointing an investigation forward.

clue.text: Diseased feeble weakling with head slightly down

parts.note: mild means weak or feeble

indicators.note: the head (first letter) is moved a little lower down the word

parts.note: a weed is a weakling

explanation.surface: A sickly weakling hanging their head a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head slightly down' moves the W of WEED one place along, giving EWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildewed means affected by mildew, a fungal plant disease.

clue.text: Agreed about male going up river

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: yes signals agreement
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man rowing upstream after agreeing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses YESREM in this down clue. The Mersey is the river through Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is a river in north-west England flowing to Liverpool.

clue.text: Personal search putting two drinks together

parts.note: 'two drinks' calls for a pair; the first is a shake, a milkshake drink
to down a glass is to drink it quickly, so drinks gives down

explanation.surface: A bartender mixing two drinks into one glass, dressed up as a police frisk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two drinks' supplies both halves: a noun (shake) and a verb (down).
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is slang for a thorough search, especially of a person by police.

clue.text: Vital wrong answer must be reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the combined letters backwards

parts.note: evil means morally wrong

explanation.surface: A quizmaster insisting that a crucial wrong answer be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: EVIL plus A gives EVILA, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means full of life, which is to be alive.

clue.text: Announced model wearing ornamental accessory

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a model is a type, and wearing means in, so the phrase gives type in

explanation.surface: A fashion model on the catwalk wearing a decorative accessory, as announced by the compere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' makes TYPE IN (model + wearing) sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiepin is a decorative pin that holds a necktie in place, an ornament of menswear.

clue.text: Expeditions scared relaxed American dons

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the anagrammed letters wrap around the other piece
relaxed means loosened, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous US traveller calms down as they set off on journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' rearranges the fear word and 'dons' wraps it round the American; 'dons' looks like university teachers but means puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusades were medieval military expeditions to the Holy Land; the word now covers any campaign.

clue.text: No person having divine protection with shift in A&E

indicators.note: a shift in A and E means those two letters trade places in the name

parts.note: Daniel was protected by God in the lions' den

explanation.surface: A hospital worker in casualty claims nobody on shift has divine protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift in A&E' swaps the A and E of DANIEL; A&E looks like the hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is saying no to something, a refusal or contradiction.

clue.text: Many show signs of uncertainty in common sense

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: nous is common sense
um and er are hesitations showing uncertainty

explanation.surface: Plenty of people hesitating despite being sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: UM and ER are two hesitation noises, together UMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, so many.

clue.text: Constant work cutting off raised route

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant (as the speed of light)

indicators.note: cutting means the word goes inside, splitting the other

parts.note: off means away, as in 'be off'
to use something is to work it

explanation.surface: Continuous roadworks block off an elevated road.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road or path raised above low wet ground or water.

clue.text: Person is embroiled in false religion

indicators.note: embroiled in means caught up inside another piece

parts.note: sham means false or fake
a man is a person

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a bogus cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamanism is a belief system centred on shamans who mediate with the spirit world.

clue.text: One might pin down runner in flight

definitions.text: One might pin down runner in flight

parts.words: One might pin down runner in flight
parts.note: the runner is a strip of stair carpet and the flight is a flight of stairs, not an escaping athlete

explanation.surface: Someone tackling a fleeing runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' and 'flight' suggest a chase; they are carpet and stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair rod is a metal bar holding a carpet runner against the back of each step.

clue.text: Putting time into designs for English dresses

indicators.note: putting one letter in place of another signals a letter swap
into marks where the new letter goes, inside the word for designs
for means in place of, naming the letter replaced

parts.note: to compose is to design or create, so designs gives composes

explanation.surface: A dressmaker working against the clock on outfits for an English client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting ... into ... for' swaps T in for the last E of COMPOSES. 'Dresses' is the gardening verb, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To compost a bed is to dress it, spreading compost over soil as a dressing.

clue.text: Two-thirds preserved, Cervantes novel in vault

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new order
keeping two-thirds means only the first six of nine letters survive

explanation.surface: Part of a Cervantes novel kept safe in a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds preserved' keeps CERVAN; 'novel' rearranges it. 'novel' looks like a book by Cervantes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavern is a large cave, and a vault is an arched chamber, so the two overlap.

clue.text: Following wolf and ominous bears

indicators.note: bears means carries within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A list of menacing animals: wolf, and ominous bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals but means carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandom is a following, the community of devoted fans of something.

clue.text: Folly and woe with son becoming married

indicators.note: becoming means one letter turns into another

parts.note: woe means sadness

explanation.surface: Marriage as a foolish, miserable decision after having a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' changes the first S of SADNESS to M.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness can mean foolishness, as in 'it would be madness to try'.

clue.text: As originally stated, very bad time with all getting reductions

indicators.note: each of the three words is reduced by losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Reporting an awful period word for word, though everyone suffered cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all getting reductions' trims each of VERY, BAD and TIME, leaving VER, BA and TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means word for word, exactly as first spoken or written.

clue.text: Misshapen deal provided recalled, cut from fir tree

indicators.note: misshapen means badly formed, so the letters are put out of shape
cut from means these letters are removed from the following word
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A twisted plank, taken back, cut from a fir tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns IF to FI, which 'cut from' FIR leaves R; 'Misshapen' gives ALDE from DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing near water.

clue.text: Open jail was adequate

parts.note: can is slang for jail
did, as in 'that did', means was enough

explanation.surface: A prison described as open and good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid person is frank and open, hiding nothing.

clue.text: Beginning to gather Romeo pulled

indicators.note: to gather means to collect inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: dawn means a beginning, as in the dawn of an era
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo starting to woo someone with a strong pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn is the past participle of draw, meaning pulled or hauled.

clue.text: Huge epidemic avoided by half of the French

indicators.note: avoided by means these letters are left out

parts.note: demi is French for half

explanation.surface: France dodging a huge epidemic by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of the French' looks like a fraction of the French people; it is the French word for half.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means vast in scale, so huge or monumental.

clue.text: Plump sandwich

definitions.meaning: a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread

explanation.definitionFit: Round means chubby in shape, and a round is also one sandwich made from two full slices.

clue.text: Plastic altarpiece, not lead, is copy

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters are reshaped
not lead means without its first letter

explanation.surface: A church altarpiece made of plastic, and not of lead, must be a reproduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not lead' drops the A of ALTARPIECE; 'Plastic' rearranges the rest. 'lead' looks like the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to copy, to make an exact reproduction.

clue.text: Spots first-rate people entering into projects

indicators.note: entering into means going inside another word

parts.note: to project is to forecast, to predict
A, as in A1, means first-rate
men means people

explanation.surface: Top-class people joining projects find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' is the tight-spot sense: awkward situations.
explanation.definitionFit: Predicaments are difficult situations, or tight spots one finds oneself in.
